# SCSS references from theme.json

Generate an SCSS partial containing references to the CSS properties defined by
your theme:

```scss
// Generated by theme-json. Do not edit.
$wp--preset--color--primary: var(--wp--preset--color--primary);
$wp--preset--font-size--body: var(--wp--preset--font-size--body);
```

Use the partial in your Sass build:

```scss
@use "tokens" as theme;

.button {
  color: theme.$wp--preset--color--primary;
  font-size: theme.$wp--preset--font-size--body;
}
```

Sass preserves `var(...)` in the resulting CSS. WordPress supplies the values at
runtime, including variations and scoped overrides. These aliases do not declare
CSS properties or make block-scoped properties global. They cannot supply
resolved values to Sass arithmetic or functions such as `color.adjust()`.

Both workflows below work with local (`vendor/bin/theme-json`) and global
(`theme-json`) installations. See [installation and autoloading](05-cli-autoloading.md).

## Generate automatically with dump

Add `ScssOutput` to the callable returned by the entrypoint:

```php
<?php

// theme.json.php

use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\Attribute\ScssOutput;
use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\ThemeJson;

return #[ScssOutput(path: 'assets/scss', filename: '_tokens.scss')]
static function (ThemeJson $themeJson): void {
    $themeJson->settings()->color()->addColor('primary', 'Primary', '#2457ab');
    $themeJson->settings()->typography()->addFontSize('body', 'Body', '1rem');
};
```

Every `theme-json dump` now generates both `theme.json` and
`assets/scss/_tokens.scss`. The exporter reads the final configuration, including
values supplied directly through `ThemeJson::set()`, presets, and configurators.

`path` is a directory relative to the declaring entrypoint. Absolute directories
also work. `filename` is optional and must end in `.scss`, without directory
components. The default is `_theme.scss` for `theme.json.php`.
Missing destination directories are created when writing.

Combine the attribute with `Autoload` and `Pipeline` when using configuration classes:

```php
<?php

// theme.json.php

use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\Attribute\Autoload;
use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\Attribute\ScssOutput;
use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\Pipeline;
use MyTheme\Configuration\Colors;

return #[Autoload('config')] #[ScssOutput('assets/scss')]
static function (Pipeline $pipeline): void {
    $pipeline->process([Colors::class]);
};
```

`Colors` is your class implementing `ConfiguratorInterface`, as described in the
[autoloading guide](05-cli-autoloading.md).

### Style variations

Each entrypoint opts in independently. Root SCSS attributes are not inherited:

```php
<?php

// styles/dark.json.php

use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\Attribute\ScssOutput;
use ItalyStrap\ThemeJsonGenerator\ThemeJson;

return #[ScssOutput('../assets/scss')]
static function (ThemeJson $themeJson): void {
    $themeJson->settings()->color()->addColor('primary', 'Primary', '#a8c8ff');
};
```

This writes `styles/dark.json` and `assets/scss/_dark.scss`. An entrypoint named
`dark.high-contrast.json.php` defaults to `_dark.high-contrast.scss`.
Each partial reflects its own input, without merging the root theme or other
variations. Shared aliases can remain identical across variations because their
CSS values are resolved at runtime.

### Command-line overrides

```shell
# Enable export for every selected entrypoint, overriding attribute destinations.
theme-json dump --scss=assets/scss

# Generate only this variation and its configured SCSS output.
theme-json dump --file=styles/dark.json

# Suppress all SCSS export for this invocation.
theme-json dump --no-scss

# Execute configuration and report planned files without writing them.
theme-json dump --scss=assets/scss --dry-run
```

Precedence is `--no-scss`, then `--scss`, then the entrypoint attribute. Without an
attribute or flag, `dump` generates no SCSS. `--scss` takes a directory and uses
default filenames even when attributes specify custom filenames. Relative flag
paths resolve from the working directory, including when `--path` selects a
different theme directory.

Selected entrypoints must have distinct output paths. Variations with identical
basenames need separate destinations or explicit filenames. Conflicting paths,
including aliases through directory symlinks, fail before the generator writes
JSON or SCSS.

## Generate from existing JSON

No PHP entrypoint, project autoloader, `style.css`, or WordPress installation is
required. This command reads JSON without executing project PHP:

```shell
theme-json scss --input=theme.json --output=assets/scss/_tokens.scss
theme-json scss --input=styles/dark.json --output=assets/scss/_dark.scss
```

`--input` defaults to `theme.json` in the working directory. `--output` defaults
to `_<input-name>.scss` beside the input: `styles/dark.json` produces
`styles/_dark.scss`. Explicit relative paths use the working directory.
The source JSON is never rewritten.

```shell
# Report the destination without creating files or directories.
theme-json scss --output=assets/scss/_tokens.scss --dry-run

# CI: exit 0 when current, 1 when missing, stale, or invalid. Never write.
theme-json scss --output=assets/scss/_tokens.scss --check
```

`--check` cannot be combined with `--dry-run`. It compares the entire expected
file, including the generated header. Run export normally to refresh stale
output. It checks SCSS against the supplied JSON, not JSON against PHP entrypoints.

## Coverage and file behavior

The exporter includes these explicit preset collections at the root and under
`settings.blocks`:

| Settings path | CSS property prefix |
| --- | --- |
| `color.palette` | `--wp--preset--color--` |
| `color.gradients` | `--wp--preset--gradient--` |
| `color.duotone` | `--wp--preset--duotone--` |
| `typography.fontSizes` | `--wp--preset--font-size--` |
| `typography.fontFamilies` | `--wp--preset--font-family--` |
| `typography.textShadowPresets` | `--wp--preset--text-shadow--` |
| `spacing.spacingSizes` | `--wp--preset--spacing--` |
| `shadow.presets` | `--wp--preset--shadow--` |
| `dimensions.aspectRatios` | `--wp--preset--aspect-ratio--` |
| `dimensions.dimensionSizes` | `--wp--preset--dimension--` |
| `border.radiusSizes` | `--wp--preset--border-radius--` |

It also flattens nested `settings.custom` values, exports explicit root layout
`contentSize` and `wideSize` variables, and exports individual root padding sides
when `useRootPaddingAwareAlignments` is enabled. Support for each property on a
live site depends on its WordPress version; duotone variables may depend on block usage.

Only information in the supplied configuration is exported. WordPress defaults,
parent-theme inheritance, generated spacing scales, site-editor overrides,
plugin filters, and declarations embedded in CSS strings are not resolved.
Declare explicit presets/custom settings when they need SCSS aliases.

Output is sorted and deduplicated, uses LF line endings, and preserves modification
time when content is unchanged. Different names that normalize to the same
property within one collection are rejected. An empty configuration produces a
valid partial containing just the generated-file comment.

Generated files are replaced atomically. Keep handwritten SCSS in separate files.
Output must be a regular `.scss` file; file symlinks are rejected. Missing or
malformed JSON, invalid names, and destination errors produce a nonzero exit code.

Run export before compiling Sass in development and CI. The workflow copied by
`workflow:init` already invokes `dump`, so SCSS attributes also run there. The
template includes a commented standalone `scss` step and SCSS staging examples.
Enable the standalone step when needed, then uncomment and adapt the staging
paths to commit your generated SCSS. By default, the template stages JSON only.
